[00:00:00.516] Hello everyone, welcome back to this course on engineering chemistry. We will continue with module 5 on energy storage devices and we'll discuss about fuel cells. In today's class, we are going to learn about hydrogen oxygen alkaline fuel cell
[00:00:19.844] The principle, construction and working, the advantages and the disadvantages. Alkaline fuel cells as the name suggests, the electrolyte which we are going to use is going to be an alkali.
[00:00:36.708] If you remember when we talked about fuel cells in general, we use a fuel at the anode and an oxidant at the cathode, and there is an electrolyte.
[00:00:50.212] So when we talk of alkaline fuel cell, alkali is used as the electrolyte, and the most commonly used alkali is KOH. These are low temperature fuel cells and they operate at about 100 degrees centigrade.
[00:01:11.012] Most common oxid which is used at the cathode is oxygen. Oxygen reduction is a very slow process. But if we use alkaline electrolytes,
[00:01:29.764] As compared to acid electrolytes, it is found that the oxygen reduction is much more rapid in alkaline electrolytes. And because of that, we need not use noble metal catalysts.
[00:01:48.132] Oxygen reduction or hydrogen oxidation. Hydrogen oxidation which happens at the anode or oxygen reduction which happens at the cathode being slow processes we need to use catalysts.
[00:02:02.564] But because it is faster, the oxygen reduction is faster in the alkaline electrolyte as compared to acid electrolyte, we can use non noble metal electrocatalysts. But
[00:02:19.492] One problem with alkaline fuel cells is that carbon containing fuels cannot be used as when they undergo oxidation, carbon dioxide is formed as a product.
[00:02:35.140] Now this reacts with the electrolyte KOH and it forms K2CO3.
[00:02:42.756] This K2CO3 is going to block the electrodes, the electrode pathways, and therefore this reduces the efficiency of the cell. The reaction would be carbon dioxide, which is formed by the due to the oxidation of
[00:02:59.328] carbon containing fuels with KOH is going to give you K2 CO3 plus H two O.
[00:03:08.004] Let us discuss the construction of such a fuel cell. Now we will take the example of hydrogen oxygen fuel cell, which is the most common type of alkaline fuel cell.
[00:03:27.236] used and has many applications and the electrolyte obviously is going to be an alkali. So just by saying that we are going to use hydrogen, oxygen, alkaline fuel cell, we can easily make out that
[00:03:45.508] At the anode it will be hydrogen which is going to be used. At the cathode we will use oxygen and the electrolyte is going to be an alkali.
[00:03:58.916] So we can see here the fuel which we are using is hydrogen gas. The oxidant which we use is oxygen.
[00:04:08.260] and the electrolyte is KOH that is 30 to 45% of KOH is used. But one thing we need to note here that the KOH used has to be warm. We'll discuss the reason in the upcoming slides.
[00:04:27.332] These are the electroactive materials. Hydrogen and oxygen are the electroactive materials, but we also need electrodes.
[00:04:36.356] So the anode that is where hydrogen is being supplied as the fuel, it is porous carbon impregnated with the platinum catalyst and at the cathode we have
[00:04:50.128] porous carbon impregnated with silver catalyst. So at the cathode we have the oxygen which is being supplied at the anode we have the fuel which is being supplied and we have electrolyte that is KOH.

Transcript block 2 (source interval 000300-000599 seconds):

[00:05:17.892] for any galvanic cell for any cell for that matter we always start with the anode. So what is being used at the anode? Hydrogen because hydrogen has to undergo oxidation and at the anode the process is always oxidation. So hydrogen is used and we know that we are using
[00:05:35.664] carbon electrodes which are impregnated with platinum. So we will put the platinum here and then comes the electrolyte. So here we have KOH as the electrolyte and then coming to the cathode side we are using oxygen as the cathodic electroactive material and the
[00:05:54.512] Carbon electrode is impregnated with silver. So the cell representation is going to be written like this hydrogen in contact with platinum, which is in contact with KH and that is again in contact with silver and finally it is in contact with oxygen.
[00:06:10.820] So let us see how we are going to draw this in a diagram. So as we know fuel cells there are three compartments. One compartment is the anodic compartment where we let in the fuel. And we also have a
[00:06:28.516] exit for the excess fuel and on the cathode side that is the other compartment where we have the cathode here is the entry for air or oxygen in this case and then there is also an exit point for the excess air or oxygen.
[00:06:48.480] and in the center we have the electrolyte that is the KOH which is being used.
[00:06:56.644] And apart from that we have the electrodes which are shown here that is the anode and this side is the cathode. So in this particular case the anode will be carbon electrode impregnated with platinum and here we have
[00:07:12.816] the carbon electrode which is impregnated with silver.
[00:07:20.100] Let us understand the working of such a cell. Now at the annual, what do we have?
[00:07:27.440] When we say working, we are basically going to understand the reactions which are taking place at the anode and cathode and the overall reaction. So at the anode we know that we are supplying hydrogen as the fuel and then it is coming in contact with the electrolyte.
[00:07:45.104] So here we have the electrolyte that is QH. So hydrogen reacts with
[00:07:50.176] OH minus and it is going to form water and two electrons are given out here because it's a oxidation reaction. And then at the cathode, these electrons are getting absorbed. So we have oxygen which we are supplying at the
[00:08:06.432] cathode here. So oxygen is going to react with water and take up these two electrons. So it's a reduction reaction and it is going to give back two OH minus. So
[00:08:18.864] Overall reaction when you add up these two reactions the half cell reactions they are known as the anode and the cathode, we find that it is hydrogen plus half O2 is giving you water. So basically it is just combustion of hydrogen which is taking place in the fuel cell.
[00:08:38.564] But what we have done is we have separated the
[00:08:43.120] oxidation and the reduction reaction into separate compartments. So as a result what happens is when hydrogen undergoes oxidation electrons are generated. These electrons move through the external wire and they are taken up at the cathode because of the
[00:09:00.752] reduction of oxygen happening here. So this way by the separating the reactions into anode and cathode just like we do for any galvanic cell, we have been able to have the stream of electrons flowing and therefore we can generate power from this cell.
[00:09:17.792] So what exactly happens, these reactions, how do they take place? So we know that hydrogen, the fuel,
[00:09:25.312] is being given from here so let us say it is hydrogen here in this case so hydrogen or any fuel for that matter is given here in this case we are talking of hydrogen oxygen fuel cell so hydrogen is being given here and it diffuses through the anode and
[00:09:42.960] Hence, it is very important that the anode has to be
[00:09:49.476] porous in nature. So hydrogen diffuses through the anode and it gets adsorbed on the electrode surface. So if it is porous obviously the surface area will be more and since the catalyst is also present over there we can

[00:10:07.136] Expedite the reaction. So when this hydrogen gets in and it reacts with the it gets absorbed on the electrode, it reacts with OH minus to form water. So water is getting formed at the anodic reaction, and you can see here that that
[00:10:24.816] vent has been provided here for the water to escape. Now here when the uh along with the excess of hydrogen water also escapes from here. In some cells we find that there is a vent provided over here and from here the water escapes.
[00:10:44.240] So it doesn't matter, it can be here or here, basically it is getting formed uh during the anodic reaction. So at the exit we find that there is excess of the fuel that is hydrogen and water which is getting uh being removed from here.
[00:10:59.460] Now at the cathode, similarly we have oxygen which is coming in from the
[00:11:05.712] uh this vent and then it is going to also diffuse through the cathode. So the cathode also has to be porous in nature. Whenever we make any fuel cells it is very essential that the electrodes have to be porous in nature because they have
[00:11:23.440] to absorb the fuel the oxidant and also the catalyst is present on the electrode. So therefore the hydrogen oxygen is getting ads at the
[00:11:34.304] uh cathode surface and it gets reduced to OH minus ions. So these OH minus ions are going to move here and again H2 is going to react with the OH minus and water is getting formed. So overall reaction we have hydrogen and oxygen is giving you water.
[00:11:53.284] So the product water now which is getting formed if it is not allowed to be removed from the cell then it is going to dilute the cage.
[00:12:08.452] Therefore, what we do is we operate the cell at 100 degrees so that the water which is formed from KOH can be it is going to escape as steam. Therefore,
[00:12:24.608] Because this water which is getting formed is obviously going to dilute the KH and we have used a particular concentration of KH. And if the KVH gets very diluted, then the efficiency of the reaction is going to fall down. Therefore, we make sure that this excess water.
[00:12:42.288] Which is getting formed continuously is removed from the system. Hence, it is very important that water is allowed to go out of the system, and that is why we operate the cell at about 100 degrees centigrade, or in other words,
[00:12:59.856] Why we use warm KH so that water escapes as steam and we maintain the concentration of KVH which is required for that for the reaction. And one more interesting fact which you must be familiar with is that during the Apollos phase
[00:13:17.424] program the water which was uh coming out of this fuel cell was collected and the astronauts were using this water for drinking.
[00:13:30.116] Now the EMF which is generated because we are using this fuel cell basically to generate power. So the voltage which is generated happens to be 1.23 volts.
[00:13:44.132] Coming to advantages of this fuel cell, it operates at a low temperature. So because of that, corrosion of equipment which is being used in the fuel cell happens to a very
[00:13:59.536] small extent as compared to those fuel cells which are operate at a very high temperature. And alkali which is used as the electrolyte is allowing us to use a non-noble metal
[00:14:17.632] catalyst and because of that what happens is the cell is now less expensive. Now if we don't use alkali if we are using acid then we know that we have to use noble metal catalyst only and as I explained earlier oxygen reduction
[00:14:36.224] is faster in an alkaline medium as compared to an acidic medium. So we can afford to use non-mobile metal catalysts here and therefore the it will work out to be much less expensive as compared to other fuel cells.
[00:14:54.112] And there are certain disadvantages that the reactants must be free from carbon. We also saw this point that if we have carbon containing fuels, then they will undergo oxidation to form carbon dioxide, and this reacts with alkali.

Transcript block 4 (source interval 000900-001199 seconds):
[00:15:12.480] And it forms carbonates, which is going to reduce the efficiency of the cell. So it also means that the fuel and the oxidant, suppose we are talking of hydrogen and oxygen, then fuel and oxidant.
[00:15:27.008] which have have which are used has has to be free of carbon compounds. And other problem is that since we are using electrolyte which is a liquid, then that could pose some handling problems. So we have advantages as well as disadvantages.
[00:15:46.640] And depending on the application where we are going to use this fuel cell, we will uh decide which type of fuel cell is suitable or whether this fuel cell is suitable for that particular
